paragraph: Single-family is the core of Elmwood Park with 41 sales over six months at a median of $625,000, and the typical sale is a three-bedroom cape with two baths, with some ranches and colonials in the mix. Sale-to-list ratio came in at 1.02 with two thirds of homes going above asking and a median of 20 days on market, so buyers should expect competition on the good ones. Prices ran from $320,000 to $1,400,000, a wide spread for a town this size, and the median is the number to anchor on. Two-families are the standout tier: 13 sales at a median of $900,000, a 1.07 sale-to-list ratio, and over 90 percent selling above asking in a median of 17 days. Sellers are dictating terms in that category. Condos and townhouses are thin at 8 sales with a median of $449,000, selling right at list in about three weeks, which is balanced by comparison. Monthly medians bounce around on samples of four to nine sales, so read those as noise, not direction. Volume built steadily from February into July, which is the normal seasonal arc. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor is whether you want the space and yard of a cape, the rental income of a two-family, or the low-maintenance setup of a condo.
